rationale.conceptual: The method is established and well-documented: use a known many-body potential, run MD cooling, apply Honeycutt–Andersen pair analysis. No novel mathematics or custom algorithms are required; it is a standard application of existing techniques.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of two sequential stages: (1) run six short MD simulations with LAMMPS, (2) post-process trajectories to compute pair fractions. All tools are open-source, and the I/O is straightforward (CSV output). No complex dependency management or multi‑tool orchestration.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires running constant-pressure MD simulations for aluminium glass at six cooling rates and extracting Honeycutt–Andersen pair fractions. The pair analysis is a standard method in amorphous metals, and the simulation scale (500 atoms) is tiny. Implementation is straightforward with LAMMPS and a short post-processing script. No new algorithms are needed, and the pipeline has only two main stages.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Only 500 aluminium atoms are simulated for a few thousand timesteps per cooling rate; total input and intermediate data volume is negligible. The calculation is comfortably handled on a single CPU core with minimal RAM.
